screens.title: From code to a result
screens.description: A Python program calculates the average, with source and successful output in the same workspace.

screens.title: Connect a line to a value
screens.description: Stepping creates a new pause snapshot, so learners can connect an expression to its result.

screens.description: The finished drawing is generated by Python, then rendered by Browser Coder’s own Turtle canvas.

screens.title: Follow the drawing back to its source
screens.description: Replay controls expose the recorded command sequence and highlight the line that produced the selected step.

films.title: Run it. Pause it. Understand it.
films.description: Follow an actual Python run into a breakpoint, inspect a new variable, compare pause snapshots, and finish the session.

chapters.title: Run the program
chapters.description: Run Python and read the actual result in the output panel.

chapters.title: Pause at a breakpoint
chapters.description: Pause before the average is calculated. Inspect the values already in memory.

chapters.title: Inspect a new value
chapters.description: Step over one line. The new average appears as 84.0.

chapters.title: Compare pause history
chapters.description: Look back at an earlier snapshot, then return to the live paused state.

chapters.title: Finish cleanly
chapters.description: Continue the real program. Session controls clear when execution finishes.

films.title: From a loop to a drawing
films.description: Run a Python Turtle program, replay its drawing commands, and inspect a recorded step alongside the source.

chapters.title: Draw with Python
chapters.description: A short loop creates a geometric drawing through real Python Turtle commands.

chapters.title: Replay the drawing
chapters.description: Replay recorded drawing commands alongside the Python line responsible for each step.

chapters.title: Inspect a drawing step
chapters.description: Scrub the replay to inspect an earlier drawing state. This replays output; it does not rerun Python.
